Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:10:1.hebrew: נימא כתנאי - הא דרב, דאמר: המקדש במלוה אינה מקודשת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:10:1.english: Let us say [it is subject to a dispute between] tanna’im - [This refers to] that [statement] of Rav, who said: "One who betroths [a woman] with a loan, she is not betrothed."

Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:10:2.english: And he authorized her against them - He wrote for her an authorization against them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:12:1.hebrew: נקנות במסירה - אינו צריך לכתוב שטר מכירה על השטר שהוא מוכר לו, אלא משמסר לו שטר שיש לו על אחרים לזכות בו, נתחייב הלוה לפורעם לזה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:12:1.english: Are acquired by delivery - He does not need to write a deed of sale for the promissory note that he is selling him; rather, once he has handed over to him a promissory note that he holds against others for him to acquire it, the borrower becomes obligated to repay them to this [buyer].

Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:12:2.hebrew: בין שכתב - לו שטר מכירה עליו ולא מסר לו שטר החוב, ובין שמסר לו שטר החוב ולא כתב לו שטר מכירה עליו — לא קנה. וה"נ שמסר לה שטר החוב, אע"פ שלא כתב לה שטר מכירה עליו: מ"ד מקודשת אית ליה דרבי, ומר לית ליה דרבי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:12:2.english: Whether one wrote - [That is, whether he wrote] a deed of sale for it to him, but did not hand over the promissory note to him; or whether he handed over the promissory note to him, but did not write a deed of sale for it to him — he has not acquired [it]. And here too, [the case is] that he handed over the promissory note to her, even though he did not write a deed of sale for it to her: the one who says [she is] betrothed holds in accordance with [the view of] Rabbi, and the [other] Master does not hold in accordance with [the view of] Rabbi.

Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:14:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא דכ"ע לית להו דרבי - והכא בשמסר וכתב מיירי, אלא שכתב לה: ״קני לך האי שטר״, ולא כתב לה: ״קני לך כל שעבודא דאית ביה״. מאן דאמר אינה מקודשת — כרב פפא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:14:1.english: And if you wish, say that everyone does not hold like Rabbi - And here, it is dealing with [a case where] he transferred [the promissory note] and wrote [a deed of transfer], but he wrote to her: “Acquire for yourself this [promissory] note,” and he did not write to her: “Acquire for yourself all the liens that are in it.” The one who says [she is] not betrothed [holds] in accordance with Rav Pappa.

Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:15:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא דכ"ע לית להו דרבי - והכא בשמסר וכתב מיירי, אלא שכתב לה: ״קני לך האי שטר״, ולא כתב לה: ״קני לך כל שעבודא דאית ביה״. מאן דאמר אינה מקודשת — כרב פפא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:15:1.english: And if you wish, say that everyone does not hold like Rabbi - And here, it is dealing with [a case where] he transferred [the promissory note] and wrote [a deed of transfer], but he wrote to her: “Acquire for yourself this [promissory] note,” and he did not write to her: “Acquire for yourself all the liens that are in it.” The one who says [she is] not betrothed [holds] in accordance with Rav Pappa.

Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:15:2.hebrew: דכולי עלמא אית להו דרב פפא - וכי אמר ר"מ מקודשת — בשכתב לה כו', והכא בדשמואל קא מיפלגי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:15:2.english: Everyone holds in accordance with Rav Pappa - And when Rabbi Meir said: “[She is] betrothed,” [it is in a case] where he wrote to her, etc., and here they disagree with regard to [the statement] of Shmuel.

Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:1:1.hebrew: הרי היא כפקדון - דאם נשתייר, אין; לא נשתייר, לא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:1:1.english: It is like a deposit - That if [the value of a peruta] remained, yes, [she is betrothed]; [if] it did not remain, no, [she is not betrothed].

Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:1:2.hebrew: אבל דכ"ע המקדש במלוה - שישנה בעין, מקודשת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:1:2.english: But everyone agrees that one who betroths with a loan - that is [still] intact, she is betrothed.

Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:2:1.hebrew: ותסברא מתרצתא היא - דקתני: במלוה, אע"פ שלא נשתייר — מקודשת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:2:1.english: And do you understand [that] it is properly explained? - For it teaches: "With a loan, even though [the value of a peruta] did not remain, she is betrothed."

Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:3:1.hebrew: אי דקביל עליה אחריות - שאם יגנב, תשלמנו לו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:3:1.english: If she accepted responsibility upon herself - That if it is stolen, she will pay it to him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:3:2.hebrew: היינו מלוה - כיון שנגנב ונתחייבה בו, נמצא מלוה אצלה. וכיון דתנא במלוה: אע"פ שלא נשתייר — מקודשת, פקדון נמי שלא נשתייר — תתקדש ביה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:3:2.english: It is a loan - Since it was stolen and she became liable for it, it turns out to be a loan in her possession. And since [the Tanna] taught regarding a loan: "Even though [the value of a peruta] did not remain, she is betrothed," [for] a deposit as well, where [the value of a peruta] did not remain, she should be betrothed by it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:3:3.hebrew: אלא דלא קביל עליה אחריות - וכי איגנוב, לא אחייבא ביה; אבל קבלה עליה אחריות, מקודשת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:3:3.english: Rather, that she did not assume responsibility for it - And when it was stolen, she is not liable for it; but [if] she assumed responsibility for it, [she is] betrothed.

Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:3:4.hebrew: אדתני - במלוה, נפלוג בפקדון גופיה, דיש פקדון שאפי' לא נשתייר כלום, מקודשת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:3:4.english: Rather than teaching - [about] a loan, let him distinguish within the deposit itself, for there is a deposit [where] even if nothing remained, she is betrothed.

Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:4:1.hebrew: אלא - על כרחך, בדקבלה עליה אחריות קתני, דאם לא נשתייר — אינה מקודשת, דמלוה היא, והמקדש במלוה אינה מקודשת; וכי נשתייר — מקודשת בההיא שיור. וגבי מלוה תריץ הכי: אע"פ שנשתייר, אינה מקודשת — משום דלהוצאה ניתנה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:4:1.english: Rather - Perforce, [the baraita] teaches [the case of a deposit where] she assumed financial responsibility for it, so that if [the value of a peruta] did not remain, she is not betrothed, for it is a loan, and one who betroths [a woman] with a loan, she is not betrothed; and when [the value of a peruta] remained, she is betrothed with that remainder. And regarding a loan, resolve [the baraita] like this: “Even though [the value of a peruta] remained, she is not betrothed” — because [a loan] is given to be spent.

Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:5:1.hebrew: במאי קמיפלגי - אי בלהוצאה ניתנה פליגי, סוף סוף כתנאי אמרה רב לשמעתיה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:5:1.english: With regard to what do they disagree? - If they disagree over whether [a loan] is given to be spent, [then] ultimately, did Rav state his teaching in accordance with [a dispute between] tanna'im?

Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:5:2.hebrew: אשכחתינהו לרבנן בבי רב - מצאתי התלמידים בבית המדרש. דכל היכא דמיירי בבי רב, לאו רב ממש הוא, אלא בבית המדרש הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:5:2.english: I found the scholars in the house of Rav - I found the students in the study hall. For wherever it speaks of “the house of Rav,” it is not Rav himself, but rather it is the study hall.

Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:5:3.hebrew: וקאמרי - לעולם להוצאה ניתנה, דברי הכל. ואם שלח בה יד להוציא ממנה שוה פרוטה — הרי החזיק בהם, ואין הבעלים יכולין לחזור, והויא ליה מלוה ואינה מקודשת, ואפילו רובה בעין. והכא, בשלא הוציא ממנה כלום. ולהכי אמר ר"ש בן אלעזר מקודשת, דקסבר: מלוה שהיא כולה בעין, ברשות בעלים היא לחזרה — אם בא מלוה לחזור בו ולתובעה, חוזר. הילכך, השתא הוא דיהבה ניהליה. והוא הדין לאונסין — קיימא נמי ברשותיה, דאי מתאנסי, פטור הלוה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:5:3.english: And they were saying - In fact, [a loan] is given to be spent according to all [opinions]. And if [the borrower] put forth a hand into it to spend a peruta’s worth from it — behold, he has taken possession of them, and the owner [the lender] cannot retract, and it becomes a [regular] loan and she is not betrothed, even if most of it is [still] intact. And here, [the dispute is in a case] where [the borrower] did not spend anything from it. And for this reason Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said [that] she is betrothed, for he holds: A loan that is entirely intact is in the possession of the owner [the lender] with regard to retraction — if the lender comes to retract and demand it [back], he may retract. Therefore, it is now that he gives it to her [as betrothal money]. And the same applies to accidents — it also stands in his [the lender's] possession, so that if it is lost due to an accident, the borrower is exempt.

Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:8:1.english: One who borrows an ax - [For example,] for ten days.

Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:8:2.hebrew: ביקע בו - הויא חזקה להשתמש בו ימי שאילתו, ואין המשאיל יכול לחזור בו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:8:2.english: [If] he chops with it - It constitutes an act of acquisition [chazakah] to use it for the days of his loan, and the lender cannot retract.

Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:8:3.hebrew: לימא כתנאי אמרה - דלר' מאיר: אם ביקע בו — קנאו; לא ביקע בו — לא קנאו. ולת"ק: אפילו לא ביקע בו נמי, דמלוה אינו ברשות בעלים לחזרה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:8:3.english: Let us say that he stated it in accordance with [a dispute between] tanna’im - For according to Rabbi Meir, if he chopped with it, he has acquired it; [if] he did not chop with it, he has not acquired it. And according to the first tanna, even [if] he did not chop with it [he has acquired it] as well, for a loan is not in the possession of the owner with regard to retraction.

Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:9:1.hebrew: דלא הדרה בעינא - הילכך, כיון דרשאי הלוה ליקח בהן סחורה, מיד הויא ליה ברשותיה, ואין המלוה יכול לחזור; שהרי לא לכך הלוהו — לקבל מעות הללו עצמן, אלא מעות אחרים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 47b:9:1.english: Which is not returned intact - Therefore, since the borrower is permitted to buy merchandise with them, it is immediately in his domain, and the lender cannot retract [the loan]; for he did not lend to him for this [purpose] — to receive these very coins, but rather other coins.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 47b:11:1.hebrew: לעולם שטר חוב דאחרים - אבל שטר חוב דידה, אינה מקודשת. וא"ת: ומאי שנא? והא אידי ואידי מלוה היא! וי"ל: דודאי מלוה דידה, שקנאתו כבר ואינו נותן לה שום דבר חדש — שהרי אותם המעות היו שלה קודם הקידושין — דין הוא דאינה מקודשת; אבל כשנתן לה המלוה דאחרים, נותן לה דבר חדש שלא היה בידה קודם, אמר דמקודשת — דנהי דאין המלוה בעין, מ"מ זכות הוא לו כאילו היה בעין:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 47b:11:1.english: "Actually, a promissory note of others" - However, [in the case of] a promissory note of her own [debt], she is not betrothed. And if you say: And what is the difference? Behold, both this and that are a loan! And one can say: That certainly [in the case of] her own loan, which she has already acquired and he is not giving her anything new — for that money was already hers prior to the betrothal — it stands to reason that she is not betrothed; but when he gives her the loan of others, he is giving her something new that was not in her possession beforehand, [and therefore Rabbi Meir] says that she is betrothed — for although the loan is not physically extant, nevertheless it is an entitlement belonging to him, as though it were physically extant.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 47b:14:1.hebrew: דכ"ע לית להו דרבי - מכאן יש להוכיח דאין הלכה כרבי, מדהוה מצי למימר דכ"ע אית להו דרבי, דמסירת אותיות לחודה מהני, והכא גבי אשה נמי מיירי שמסר לה את השטר, והיינו טעמא דחכמים דאמרי אינה מקודשת — משום דקסברי דצריך לומר בפה כשמוסר לו השטר: "קני לך איהו וכל שיעבודיה", והוא לא אמר לה כך. ופליגי בדרב פפא, דכי היכי דאמר רב פפא דבעי למיכתב ליה "קני לך איהו וכל שיעבודיה", כמו כן צריך לומר הכי בפה למ"ד אותיות במסירה נקנות. ומדקאמר גמרא דכ"ע לית להו דרבי — שמע מינה דלית הלכתא כוותיה דרבי. ובפרק המוכר את הספינה (ב"ב דף עז.) יש ספרים חלוקין: אית דגרסי דהלכה דאותיות נקנות במסירה, ואית דגרסי דהלכה דאין אותיות נקנות במסירה; ומשמע הכא כההיא גירסא דאין אותיות נקנות במסירה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 47b:14:1.english: "Everyone does not hold like Rabbi" - From here there is proof that the halakha is not in accordance with Rabbi, since [the Gemara] could have said that everyone holds in accordance with [the view of] Rabbi, that delivery of documents alone is effective, and here regarding the woman it is also dealing with [a case where] he handed over the [promissory] note to her, and this is the reasoning of the Rabbis who say [that] she is not betrothed: because they hold that one must say orally when handing him the document, "Acquire it and all its liens," and he did not say this to her; and they disagree with regard to [the statement of] Rav Pappa, for just as Rav Pappa says that he needs to write to him, "Acquire it and all its liens," so too he must say this orally according to the one who holds [that] documents are acquired by delivery. And since the Gemara says "everyone does not hold like Rabbi," deduce from it that the halakha is not in accordance with Rabbi. And in the chapter [entitled] HaMokher Et HaSefinah (Bava Batra 77a), there are conflicting texts: some versions read that the halakha is that documents are acquired by delivery, and some versions read that the halakha is that documents are not acquired by delivery; and [the Gemara] here implies in accordance with that version, that documents are not acquired by delivery.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 47b:7:1.hebrew: אלא מלוה ברשות בעלים לחזרה איכא בינייהו - פ': דלת"ק דר"ש אינה מקודשת, משום דמלוה ברשות לוה קיימא; ור"ש בן אלעזר דאמר מקודשת, משום דמלוה ברשות מלוה קיימא. וא"ת: אכתי נימא רב כתנאי אמרה לשמעתיה? דהא איהו דאמר "המקדש במלוה אינה מקודשת", לא מצי סבר כר"ש בן אלעזר! וי"ל: דרב נמי סבר כוותיה, ולא תיקשי מידי; דהא דאמר רב "אינה מקודשת" — מיירי במלוה שהתחיל להוציאה, ובהא קאמר דאינה מקודשת אפילו נשתייר שוה פרוטה; ור"ש בן אלעזר לא איירי אלא במלוה שהיא עדיין בעין. ואע"ג דאמר במילתיה דר"ש "אם נשתייר ש"פ מקודשת", דמשמע אע"פ שהתחיל להוציאה — י"ל: דר"ש בן אלעזר מיירי שנגנבו או שאבדו שלא שלח בהן יד; אבל אם התחיל להוציאה — אינה מקודשת:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 47b:7:1.english: "Rather, [the issue of whether] a loan is in the possession of the owner with regard to retraction is [the difference] between them" - Explanation: According to the first tanna [who disputes] Rabbi Shimon [ben Elazar], she is not betrothed because a loan stands in the possession of the borrower; and Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, who says that she is betrothed, [holds so] because a loan stands in the possession of the lender. And if you will say: Still, let us say that Rav stated his teaching in accordance with [a dispute between] tanna’im? For since he is the one who said, "One who betroths [a woman] with a loan, she is not betrothed," he cannot hold in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar! And one can say: Rav also holds in accordance with him, and nothing is difficult [from this]. For that which Rav said, "She is not betrothed," is dealing with a loan that she had begun to spend, and regarding this he states that she is not betrothed even if the value of a peruta remained; whereas Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar was dealing only with a loan that is still intact. And even though it says in the statement of Rabbi Shimon [ben Elazar], "If the value of a peruta remained, she is betrothed," which implies [that she is betrothed] even though she had begun to spend it — one can say: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar is dealing with [a case where the rest] was stolen or was lost, without her having laid a hand on them [to spend them]; but if she had begun to spend them, she is not betrothed.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 47b:8:1.hebrew: אלא הא דאמר רב הונא השואל קורדום מחבירו ביקע בו קנאו - לענין שלא יוכל המשאיל לחזור בו קאמר, אבל לענין להתחייב באונסין — כי לא ביקע בו נמי חייב באונסין, כדאמר בפרק השואל (ב"מ דף צט.) דמשעת משיכה חייב באונסיה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 47b:8:1.english: "But rather, that which Rav Huna says: One who borrows an ax from his friend, [if] he chops with it he has acquired it" - [Rav Huna] is speaking with regard to [the rule] that the lender cannot renege [on the loan]; but with regard to becoming liable for unavoidable mishaps [onesin], even if he did not chop with it he is also liable for unavoidable mishaps, as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] HaSho’el (Bava Metzia 99a), that from the moment of pulling [meshikhah] he is liable for its unavoidable mishaps.
